name: audio-player
purpose: A compact player for one audio clip: play and pause, a seek bar between the current time and the duration, mute and volume, and, when asked for, a playback speed control, a download link and a transcript. It plays what the app hands it (a URL, an object URL or a `data:` URL built from base64 audio) on the browser's own audio element; it fetches and decodes nothing. It owns the generating, buffering and error states, so an AI reply that speaks, or a stored recording, looks the same everywhere.
useWhen: An AI reply that carries audio: speech generated from text, generated music or sound, an audio part of a chat message.
A voice note or recording a person attached to a message or a ticket.
Previewing one stored audio file in a detail pane or drawer.
avoidWhen: Video, or audio that needs a picture → use `DocFrame` (a captured clip) or `Embed` (a hosted player).
Recording audio or a live voice conversation → use `PromptInput` and its dictate button.
A file of any type with a type-aware fallback → use `FilePreview`.
Background or decorative sound that the reader did not ask for → do not autoplay audio; leave it out.
related: `FilePreview` — the preview of a stored file of any type; an audio file can open in an `AudioPlayer` instead.
`ChatMessage` — the message an audio reply sits in.
`Slider` — the seek and volume controls inside this component.
`IconButton` — the play, mute and download controls inside this component.
bestPractices: Build `src` once from the source the app has: a URL as it is, base64 audio as `data:<mimeType>;base64,<value>`, a `Blob` as an object URL (revoke it when the player unmounts).
Pass `duration` when the generator reports it, so the time shows before the browser has read the file.
Set `loading` while the audio is being generated, so the player holds its place in the reply instead of appearing when it is done.
Pass the text the audio speaks as `transcript`; a reader who cannot hear it reads it instead (WCAG 1.2.1).
Give each player a `title` when a message holds more than one, so each control group has its own name.
Never start playback on mount; the reader presses Play.
In a narrow column only Mute is left for the volume; the device volume covers the rest on a phone.

props.name: src
props.doc: Audio source: a URL, an object URL or a data URL built from base64 audio. Empty disables the controls.

props.name: title
props.doc: Name of the clip, shown above the controls and used as the accessible name of the control group.

props.name: duration
props.doc: Length of the clip in seconds, shown until the browser reads it from the file. Unset shows a placeholder.

props.name: transcript
props.doc: Text the audio speaks, shown in a collapsible Transcript section under the controls. Empty hides the section.

props.name: playbackRates
props.doc: Playback speeds the speed control cycles through, in order. Empty hides it; it starts at 1 when listed, else the first.

props.name: fileName
props.doc: File name the Download link saves the audio as. Empty lets the browser pick one.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The audio is still being generated or fetched: the play control shows a spinner and the other controls are disabled.

props.name: error
props.doc: Why the audio cannot play. Set, the controls are disabled and this text replaces the time.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Disables every control and applies the disabled tokens.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name of the control group when there is no `title`. Empty falls back to the catalog's Audio player.

events.name: pause
events.notes: Playback paused, by the reader or because the clip reached its end (the element's `pause` event).

events.name: retry
events.notes: Try again in the error state was pressed. The button renders only when this event has a listener; an error the audio element reported is cleared and the element loads `src` again, and the app clears or keeps `error`.
